top.para: Guidance for bring-your-own-problem build days designed around shipping something someone else can use: AI running the event, browser only, prepared cases, villagers and synthetic users, GitHub Pages, five stages, and testing the day first.

in-short.para: The format; shipping; AI runs it; browser only; cases; helpers; test it first and the loop.

format.para: Bring your laptop and a problem and build something: it starts from the participant's world; guidance drawn from many events, not one.

ship.line: Ship something someone else can use
ship.para: The hard part is a second user; design the day so everyone pushes, shares and watches someone use what they made.

ai.line: Use AI to run the event
ai.para: Know who is coming, prepare customised briefs and cases, playbooks and handouts, and draft follow-ups.

browser.para: Nothing to install, no payments on the day, no database: remove every obstacle from the first minutes.

cases.line: Cases and recipes, ready before the day
cases.para: Realistic invented spreadsheets mapped to apps with prompt recipes; easy examples that work the first time.

helpers.line: Villagers and synthetic users in the room
helpers.para: Helpers who publish and share; agents that test each app, describe it and present it.

architecture.para: No major databases, everything in the browser, published with GitHub Pages: a page that says what it does and the thing itself.

stages.para: Type and see it work; change it; share a link; a website; used by others.

test.line: Test the event before it happens
test.para: Synthetic users with participants' profiles try the onboarding, cases and recipes and report where they stuck.

loop.para: The feedback loop: build, ship, watch someone use it, change it, ship again.

limits.para: Guidance from experience; about no particular event; credits change; my interest.
